text:
laura-ic: scan-bot posted SAST+DAST bundle for pipeline run release/2026-03-20 build-8792. There's a medium vuln flagged in auth-service and a DAST timing issue on staging. Can someone confirm provenance of the scan artifacts? :eyes:

scan-bot: [auto] SAST: 1 medium, 3 low; DAST: 1 medium, 2 info. Artifacts: s3://redwood-ci/artifacts/build-8792/scans/sast.json (signed), s3://redwood-ci/artifacts/build-8792/scans/dast-report.html (unsigned). Signature: cosign.sig in same prefix.

mike-ops: I see the S3 objects. The sast.json has a cosign signature blob but dast-report.html is missing one. Did the pipeline step that uploads DAST skip signing?

tess-eng: yep, pipeline changed last week to stream DAST to ephemeral storage to save space, we probably missed the signing hook. @mike-ops can we add signing to the dast upload step?

mike-ops: We can. Quick question: for RBAC, which role should be allowed to create signatures? Currently only deploy-key-service has kms:Sign, not CI runners.

anuj-sec: We intentionally keep signing restricted to the signing service that uses HSM-backed keys. CI runners should push unsigned artifacts and call the signing service via an authenticated webhook to produce the final signature. Keeps private key off runners.

laura-ic: That workflow is fine, but the SAST was signed directly by the runner (I checked cosign metadata) — looks like it used a different key, not the HSM one. We should trace who provisioned that key.

mike-ops: Hmm. Snapshot of cosign metadata: issuer=ci-runner-01, key-id=ci-key-2025. That key is in KMS under project/ci-keys. I thought we retired ci-key-2025.

anuj-sec: ci-key-2025 should have been disabled during the rotation last month. I'll check KMS audit logs. If it was used, that's an IAM/RBAC issue that needs immediate triage.

sre-bot: [audit] 2401234602: KMS.Encrypt called by serviceAccount:ci-runner-01@redwood.iam; 2401234615: KMS.Sign called by serviceAccount:ci-runner-01@redwood.iam; key=projects/ci-keys/ci-key-2025.

anuj-sec: Confirmed: key was still enabled and had an outdated binding allowing the CI runners group. I will immediately rotate/disable that key and create a short-lived key to re-sign necessary SAST artifacts where needed.

laura-ic: Before we change keys, need to preserve evidence chain for vuln triage. The auth-service finding references line numbers in the signed artifact. We need both signed and unsigned copies + the signature to validate integrity.

mike-ops: I'll snapshot s3://redwood-ci/artifacts/build-8792 to a read-only bucket and add lifecycle hold. Also will export current KMS key version metadata and store a tamper-evident record in the incidents bucket.

tess-eng: For immediate patching: auth-service change is small (missing null check) and we've got a deploy candidate branch ready. Do we treat this as a release-blocker given it's medium?

anuj-sec: Treat as P2 (needs fix in next release) unless exploitability surface increases. But ensure reviewers verifying fix have access to original signed scan to compare baselines. Also run a regression DAST on staging after the fix.

laura-ic: Assigning owners: @tess-eng take patch and PR, @mike-ops handle artifact preservation + signing key rotation plan, @anuj-sec lead audit log extraction and incident note. I'll own triage thread and update security tracker ticket SEC-1371.

mike-ops: Will do. Quick ops note — adding the signing webhook to DAST upload will include a retry idempotency key to avoid double-signing. Code snippet I plan to add to the pipeline: 

```bash
# upload then request signature
aws s3 cp dast-report.html s3://redwood-ci/artifacts/build-8792/scans/dast-report.html \
&& curl -X POST https://signing.internal/api/sign \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SIGNING_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"s3_path":"s3://redwood-ci/artifacts/.../dast-report.html","request_id":"$CI_RUN_ID"}'

# signing service will return cosign.sig and cosign.pub for verification
```

anuj-sec: That looks good. For KMS rotation: I'll create a new key with strict IAM (signing-service role only), rotate the pipeline to call the signing-service, then disable ci-key-2025. We'll document the key provenance in the incident ticket with the audit log snippets.

laura-ic: One more ask — update the pre-merge gate so that any signed artifact must have a signature with an allowed keyset. We should reject PR merges if the artifact signature key-id is not in allowlist.json.

tess-eng: I can add that check to the GH action that validates scan uploads before marking the PR as green. Simple JSON check against allowlist.

mike-ops: I'll help by publishing allowlist.json from a central config repo and adding a small verification binary to the pipeline.

scan-bot: [auto] DAST re-run scheduled on staging after patch merge: run-2026-03-20-8793.

laura-ic: Great. Wrap-up: preserve artifacts (mike), rotate/lock keys and extract logs (anuj), patch + PR (tess). I'll file SEC-1371 with timelines and add this thread as evidence. If anything changes escalate to incident-oncall. :white_check_mark:
